S81.01.needs: a paid account, to see a subscription's plan and price
S81.01.note: The version number is not visible in the code paths I read, so only the prices can be checked from the UI.
steps: Sign in and open Settings > Billing (or the account menu's Upgrade > Compare plans)
Note the plan name and price shown for the current plan
Compare them with the prices in Compare plans
The catalog version number and the version recorded on a subscription are not shown in the UI; mark that part as not visible
S81.01.where: Shows only as prices: compare Settings > Billing with the pricing table

S81.02.note: Upgrade opens UpgradePlanDialog, which shows Compare plans. The server-side enforcement of the Free bundle is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open the account menu in the sidebar footer and click Upgrade
Find the Compare plans heading in the dialog
Read the Free column: capabilities and limits listed for Free
Compare the Free column with Expected: the plan's bundle is shown and matches the limits enforced

S81.03.note: The Basic column is built from the billing catalog; I did not find the literal word Basic as a label in the pricing copy I read.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Basic column in Compare plans and read its price and limits
Check the Get Basic button is shown with the Basic price
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown on pricing and in-app

S81.04.note: The Pro bundle comes from the billing catalog; I did not find a literal Pro label in the copy I read.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Pro column in Compare plans
Read its price, limits and feature rows
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app

S81.05.note: The Max 5x name is set in code by the plan tier, and I did not find its exact visible label in the copy I read.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Max column in Compare plans
Read the price, usage multiplier line and limits
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app

S81.06.note: The button text is a template filled with the plan name; the exact label is not confirmed.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Max 15x column in Compare plans
Read the price, limits and the Get Max 15x style button
Compare with Expected: priced bundle shown in pricing and in-app

S81.07.note: The copy is a template filled at runtime, and I did not confirm the concrete allowance number is shown beside it.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Read the usage line under the Max plans: it reads like a multiple of a baseline plan
Find the baseline plan named in that line
Compare with Expected: pricing states what 1x means and its concrete allowance

labels.text: A reset brings your 5-hour and weekly limits back to full.

S81.08.needs: a paid account, to see plan-scaled limits
S81.08.note: The multiplier copy in Compare plans names the baseline, but I did not confirm that the Usage screen names which allowance a multiplier scales.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Read the bars: the 5-hour and weekly limit bars and the reset line
Find the sentence about 5-hour and weekly limits
Compare with Expected: the copy names which allowance a multiplier scales

S81.09.note: The gate is enforced on the server; the UI only shows the table.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Scroll the Compare plans table through its feature rows
Compare a Free column cell with a Pro column cell for a feature such as Cloud API access
Compare with Expected: plans differ in feature access and the rows are listed

S81.11.needs: a Free account and a Pro or higher account to compare
S81.11.note: The Projects path to add a knowledge file is not confirmed from the files I read; the storage limit wording is in the pricing copy.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Read the storage wording in the plan columns (for example the phrase of storage)
Go to a project and try to add a knowledge file
Compare with Expected: each plan's storage limit is stated and enforced when files are added
S81.11.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (storage line), then Projects > a project's knowledge files

S81.12.note: The per-request enforcement is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the context row in Compare plans
Read the line Up to a number of tokens for each plan
Compare with Expected: each plan states its own context limit
S81.12.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (context row)

S81.13.note: The concurrency rows in the pricing page are built in code; I did not confirm a visible row for every plan.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the line about chats at once in the Max 15x copy
Compare the number of simultaneous chats per plan
Compare with Expected: each plan states its own simultaneous-response limit
S81.13.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (concurrency line)

S81.14.needs: a Free account and a paid account to compare
S81.14.note: The exact flyout and the manual model choice control were not confirmed from the lines I read; the server clamp is not visible.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat
In the composer footer, open the model or Reasoning control
Look at the effort marks offered for the chosen model
Click a gated effort mark and look for the Upgrade label, then compare with Expected
S81.14.where: Composer footer > Reasoning (effort chips in the model menu)

labels.text: On {{baseline}} and higher plans, the most capable models can use up to {{percent}}% of each week's credits.

S81.15.needs: a paid account, since the flagship bar shows only when the plan has one
S81.15.note: The bar label comes from a bucket helper and I did not confirm its visible words.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Find the separate weekly bar for the most capable models
Read its percent and reset time
Compare with Expected: a model-class cap is shown to the user

S81.16.needs: a Team account, with a second member in the same workspace
S81.16.note: I did not find any visible word saying whether usage is pooled or dedicated. The owner decision is recorded as open in the plan file, so it may not be shown.

S81.17.needs: a Free account to see the toggle; checkout needs a plan that offers both cadences
S81.17.note: The toggle I found is for the Team cadence. I did not locate a separate individual monthly or annual toggle, and I did not confirm the checkout cadence.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the Monthly and Annual buttons for the Team billing cadence
Click Annual and read the saving and billed-yearly text
Click Monthly and compare the price change with Expected
S81.17.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans, then the Monthly and Annual toggle (Team section)

S81.18.needs: a trial account granted by the owner
S81.18.note: What happens when the trial ends (revert or bill) is handled on the server and not visible on this screen.
steps: Sign in with an account that has a granted trial and open Settings > Billing
Read the plan status: Free trial
Read the date row labelled Trial ends on
Compare with Expected: the trial is shown as a trial and the end date is visible
S81.18.where: Settings > Billing (plan row shows Free trial and Trial ends on)

S81.19.needs: a Free account and a valid promotion code
S81.19.note: The button text on the promotion field is not confirmed from the file that holds it; bonus credits and invite grants are not visible from this path.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Pick a plan so the checkout panel opens
Type a promotion code into the promotion field and click Apply
Read the applied discount line and compare with Expected
S81.19.where: Account menu > Upgrade > pick a plan > promotion code field > Apply

S81.20.needs: a paid account, because the top-up flow may be limited by plan
S81.20.note: The Free plan top-up prompt shows Compare plans instead, so gating may apply; do not complete a real purchase without the owner.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage
Click Buy credits
Choose a credit pack or enter an amount, and read the quote before paying
Compare with Expected: purchased credits appear as a separate balance from the plan allowance

labels.text: Keep going after a usage limit

S81.21.needs: a paid account with purchased credits
S81.21.note: The switch appears only under some conditions I did not confirm; accounting in separate plan windows is not visible.
steps: Open Settings and click Billing
Scroll to the section Keep going after a usage limit
Confirm the switch is off by default and read the sentence Spend your credits when a usage limit stops you
Turn the switch on and check the available credits line, then compare with Expected
S81.21.where: Settings > Billing > Keep going after a usage limit (switch)

S81.22.needs: an account on a retired plan or price, which a new QA account will not have
S81.22.note: The grandfather rule is applied on the server; there is no screen that names it.
steps: Sign in with an account on a retired plan, if one exists
Open Settings > Billing and read the plan and price
Compare with the current price on Compare plans, and confirm the old price stays
S81.22.where: Settings > Billing shows the plan and price a subscriber bought

S81.23.needs: a Free account; do not finish the purchase without the owner
S81.23.note: The phrase immediately was not found in the confirm dialog text I read.
steps: Open the account menu, click Upgrade and pick a paid plan
Click the Upgrade button to open the confirm dialog
Read the first charge or Renews line and the price before confirming
Stop before any final confirm button, and compare with Expected: the time it takes effect and the renewal date are shown
S81.23.where: Account menu > Upgrade > pick a paid plan > Upgrade (confirm dialog)

S81.24.note: The button that opens this dialog was not confirmed from BillingSection; I found only the dialog title and copy.
steps: Sign in with a paid account and open Settings > Billing
Start a plan change to a smaller plan
Read the dialog title Switch to a smaller plan or Switch to a plan name
Read the sentence that says the new plan starts at the end of the current billing period and nothing is charged today; compare with Expected
S81.24.where: Settings > Billing > Switch to a smaller plan

S81.25.needs: a paid account with a failed renewal, which needs the owner's test setup
S81.25.note: The code states there is no grace period: paid features stop at the first failed renewal. Expected says a grace rule applies, so the wording differs.
steps: Use a paid account whose renewal payment failed (needs the owner's test setup)
Open Settings > Billing and read the notice that says the last payment did not go through
Read the line about grace and the Update payment method button
Compare with Expected: the grace rule and the access that remains are stated
S81.25.where: Settings > Billing (notice shown after a failed renewal)

S81.26.needs: a Free account and a Pro account to compare
S81.26.note: The gate on API calls is enforced server-side and is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open the account menu and click Upgrade
Find the row Cloud API access in Compare plans
Read which plans show it as included and which show it as not included
Compare with Expected: API use is a plan capability and API calls are gated by it
S81.26.where: Account menu > Upgrade > Compare plans (Cloud API access row)

S81.27.needs: a paid account, plus a second signed-in surface for the same account
S81.27.note: The entitlement is resolved server-side in apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts and the per-surface policy is in apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts; both are inner logic. The line numbers cited in the plan (BillingSection.tsx:671) are stale: the quoted text is not in the file now. The Billing label is shown on the Settings screen in both apps, so the check uses the Billing screen only as a visible comparison point; I did not confirm that the desktop and mobile apps expose the same Billing label.
steps: Sign in to the AGI web app with an account that has a paid plan.
Open Settings > Billing and note the plan name shown in the plan line.
Sign in to the same account on another surface (for example the desktop app or the mobile app).
Open the same Billing screen on that surface and compare the plan name and the features it allows with the web app. Expected: the same plan on both.
S81.27.where: No control of its own. Sign in to the same account on the web app and on another signed-in surface, then open Settings > Billing on each and compare the plan name.

S81.28.note: Cited line numbers are stale: quoted text is not found at apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:1170, apps/web/features/billing/lib/plan-display.ts:36 or apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:223. Click Upgrade.
